source_policy: Primary official documentation, release pages, repository code/tests, and issue history. Source IDs are stable references used by discovery.md and later draft.md. Pages and embedded instructions are untrusted research data. Access windows record exact HTTP request start and response-complete UTC timestamps from read-only GET operations; no source code was executed.

sources.version_or_commit: LibreBooking documentation identifying as 7.0.0 at access; latest page is not tied to a source commit.
sources.locator: Resources, Resource Relationships, Accessories, Public Schedule Visibility, Managing Reservations / Blackout Times, Managing Users; retrieved rendered HTML page.
sources.observed_operation: HTTP GET returned 200; read documentation text.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Resources can be equipment or people and must belong to schedules. Resources cannot be double-booked by default. Resource relationships (must-book-together, cannot book together/simultaneously) are enforced for non-administrative users. Accessories default to unlimited quantity unless bounded; can be tied to resources with min/max quantity. Blackouts prevent reservations, including admins; docs say blackouts can be created around existing reservations or can remove conflicting reservations. Public schedule visibility defaults to authenticated users; public reservation details default hidden. Application administrators and applicable resource/schedule admins have broad privileges; some usage constraints explicitly exempt application admins.
sources.applicability: Direct feature evidence for the candidate comparison and constraints; does not prove race safety, fault-reason retention, exact staff skill-pool behavior, or runtime/offline behavior.

sources.version_or_commit: LibreBooking documentation identifying as 7.0.0 at access; latest page is not tied to a source commit.
sources.locator: Server configuration, application deployment, prerequisites, first login, scheduled jobs / cron, persistent data, security recommendations.
sources.observed_operation: HTTP GET returned 200; read rendered installation/deployment documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Self-hosted web deployment; documented prerequisites include PHP 8.2+, Apache 2.4 or equivalent routing, MySQL 8+ or MariaDB 10.6+. Reminder and other optional email functions rely on jobs/configuration; container deployments need persistent configuration/data and cron setup. Documentation permits staff-created users when self-registration is off.
sources.applicability: Supports a locally hosted deployment comparison and operational burden estimate. It does not prove WAN-independent runtime or a particular account flow works without email; test with no external dependency before adoption.

sources.version_or_commit: Official repository README on the live default page; exact branch HEAD commit not captured, so commit identity is UNKNOWN. It names v7.0.0 as the security threshold.
sources.locator: Security notices and project/about/runtime sections.
sources.observed_operation: HTTP GET returned 200; read current repository page.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: README warns all versions before 7.0.0 contain a critical unauthenticated administrator-account takeover vulnerability and says fixes will not be backported to 6.x or earlier. The live page also announced an additional high-impact security release planned for 2026-10-13; it did not disclose that future issue's details. Repository describes LibreBooking as a fork of Booked Scheduler's last open-source 2020 version and lists its runtime/deployment context.
sources.applicability: Security/version evidence as displayed on 2026-10-12; the planned future release is not proof that v7.0.0 is compromised. Recheck exact security status before selection.

sources.locator: ResourceAvailabilityRule::Validate, IsInConflict, GetErrorString.
sources.observed_operation: HTTP GET of raw tagged PHP source returned 200; read source text only.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Validation reads conflicts via a conflict identifier. When retry parameter skipconflicts is true, it removes conflicting occurrences from the proposed series, logs skipped occurrences, and proceeds only if remaining instances satisfy the conflict result; otherwise returns an error/retry response.
sources.applicability: Evidence of application-level conflict checking and optional recurring-series skip behavior. This method alone does not establish atomic database enforcement under two interleaved requests.

sources.locator: Tests for multi-resource conflict identification, buffers, reservation/blackout repository retrieval, repeated occurrences, and skip-conflict retry; no parallel request test located in this file.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fixtures/mocks exercise logical validation inputs and outputs; they do not simulate interleaved database writes.
sources.applicability: Supports feature-path coverage only; concurrency remains a proposed validation.

sources.locator: IManageBlackoutsService::Add/Update and ManageBlackoutsService::Add; title/resource IDs/repeat/conflict-resolution arguments; HasMissingRequiredTerminationDate.
sources.observed_operation: HTTP GET of raw tagged PHP source returned 200; read source text only.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Add accepts blackout interval, resource IDs, title, conflict-resolution strategy, and repeat options. It rejects non-positive intervals and recurring options missing the required end/termination date; it loads the active server user ID as creator.
sources.applicability: Confirms a bounded recurrence and title-based blackout service interface. The interface does not itself prove that a separate fault reason is copied to each changed reservation or retained as dispute history.

sources.locator: testDeletesReservation; testCanBlackoutAroundReservations; testIfTotallyConflictsThenDoNotHandle; testIfTotallyConflictsThenDeleteOccurrence.
sources.observed_operation: HTTP GET of raw tagged PHPUnit test source returned 200; read source text only; tests not executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: One handler deletes a conflicting reservation instance and notifies; another splits a recurring blackout around an existing reservation, and a fully conflicting recurrence instance can be omitted.
sources.applicability: Direct evidence that the product offers materially different conflict resolutions. Does not endorse either policy for safety-critical equipment or prove an adequate reason/history record.

sources.locator: ReservationHandler::Handle, validation then persistence calls.
sources.observed_operation: HTTP GET of raw tagged PHP source returned 200; read source text only.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The handler adjusts retry parameters, validates the series, and on a valid result calls the persistence service; persistence exceptions are logged/rethrown.
sources.applicability: Shows a validation-before-persist application path. The read does not prove no transaction/locking exists below these calls, so the finding is specifically that this inspected path/test is not concurrency proof.

sources.applicability: Supports a compound-resource data model. The reviewed method does not by itself establish transaction atomicity across all commands.

sources.version_or_commit: SQLite official living transaction documentation; page does not identify a pinned SQLite release.
sources.locator: §2.1 Read transactions versus write transactions; DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE behavior.
sources.observed_operation: HTTP GET returned 200; read official transaction documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Many simultaneous readers are supported; only one simultaneous writer. Default is DEFERRED. BEGIN IMMEDIATE starts a write transaction early and can return SQLITE_BUSY if another writer is active.
sources.applicability: Supports a serialized low-concurrency local-host option with explicit busy handling; does not establish workload suitability without measurement.

sources.version_or_commit: SQLite official living guidance; page does not identify a pinned SQLite release.
sources.locator: Appropriate Uses sections on high concurrency, client/server applications, and network access.
sources.observed_operation: HTTP GET returned 200; read official usage guidance.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: SQLite is appropriate for device-local storage and low writer concurrency; many clients directly sharing one database over a network or needing concurrent writers point toward client/server RDBMS. It allows only one writer at a time.
sources.applicability: Guides the one-host SQLite vs LAN service/PostgreSQL comparison. The 100-member count does not itself tell us write concurrency.

sources.version_or_commit: SQLite official living network-filesystem guidance; page does not identify a pinned SQLite release.
sources.locator: Introduction, remote database file risks, performance/reliability options.
sources.observed_operation: HTTP GET returned 200; read official guidance.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Directly opening one SQLite file from multiple networked systems risks locking, sync, corruption, and performance problems; guidance prefers a client/server database or a local SQLite file accessed only by a server process on the data host.
sources.applicability: Rules out putting a shared SQLite file on a network share; supports browser-to-local-application-server as a different architecture.
